Melatonin has been reported to alleviate jet lag fol- lowing long flights.1-4 The most appropriate dosing schedule has yet to be determined but will depend on both the direction of travel and the distance travelled. A systematic review5 con- cluded that melatonin was effective in preventing or reducing jet lag in those travelling across 5 or more time zones, partic- ularly in an easterly direction, and especially if jet lag had been experienced previously; travellers crossing 2 to 4 time zones might also derive benefit. However, a meta-analysis6 of randomised controlled studies concluded that melatonin does not have a significant effect on sleep onset latency accompa- nying jet lag. 1. Waterhouse J, et al. Jet-lag.
